# Requirements and their evidence, in plain English

A companion to `docs/traceability_matrix.md`. The matrix says which artifacts name a criterion; this says, for the requirements the paper's claims rest on, what the requirement asks, what does it, what the formal statements actually say, and whether that is as much as the requirement asks.

How to read it:

- The sentences are written by hand from the text of the cited statements. The identifiers, criteria, files, line numbers, statement names, tools and Evidence_Items are generated from the same data as the matrix.
- Every cited statement's text is hashed. A statement that has changed since its row was written is marked **CHANGED** below and fails `cargo xtask reqdoc --check` and the verification job, until the row is read again against the new text.
- "Proven" means a tool checked the statement against the code or the model it names. It does not mean the statement says what the requirement says: that is the fifth column.
- Evidence_Item verdicts are those of the store `target/xtask-verify/evidence` when this file was generated; an item not in that store is listed without a verdict.

- 61 of the 61 requirements have a row written by hand. The other 0 have a row generated from the requirement's own user story and the matrix, marked **not yet read**: it lists what exists and judges nothing.

| **R8** Resource locking and the ceiling protocol (R8.1 to R8.10, Phase P1).<br>A Job enters a shared Resource by raising the system ceiling to the Resource's ceiling and leaves by restoring it; no two Jobs are ever inside the same Resource, a Job never waits at a lock, a Job is blocked at most once per Release for at most one critical section, and no deadlock is possible. | `Sched::lock` and `unlock` keep a stack of held Resources and the ceiling (crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/sched.rs), reached through two supervisor calls; the Generator computes each Resource's ceiling from the declaration, and the `rsk::Shared::lock` API gives the data only inside a closure (crates/rsk/src/lib.rs).<br>Statements in: `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/history.rs`, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/sched.rs`.<br>25 source files cite a criterion of R8 in the matrix (2 of the files above among them). | `lemma_no_other_holder` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/sched.rs:472`): In a valid state with a Job on top that may access Resource r, any entry of the held-Resource stack for r belongs to that Job itself: no other Job holds r.<br>`lemma_deadlock_free` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/sched.rs:286`): In every valid state: the Job on top waits for no Resource; every pending Job that is not eligible either has a Job in progress or is blocked by some Job on the stack; and a blocker is in progress and is itself blocked by nothing. A lock by the Job on top finds any existing holder entry of that Resource to be the Job's own (so it never waits); a pending Job that is not eligible is blocked by exactly the kind of holder R8.4 describes (a lower-Priority Job holding a Resource whose ceiling reaches it); a blocker itself waits for nothing, so there is no cycle; and between a lock and its matching unlock the stack of held Resources and the ceiling return to what they were. R8.6, R8.7 and R8.10 are the type system's and the Generator's, shown by compile-fail cases. | **R9** Periodic release and timer dispatch (R9.1 to R9.10, Phase P1).<br>Each periodic Task is released at its offset plus a whole number of periods, computed from the offset and period alone so that it never drifts; a Release that falls due while the previous one is still pending is discarded and counted; a Job not finished by its deadline is reported; and at the end of the declared operating duration the system enters its safe state. | The Kernel keeps one timer slot per timed event and a nominal instant per periodic Task; the timer entry serves every slot that is due (`Kernel::timer_event`, `periodic_release`, `deadline_miss` in crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/kernel.rs; the instants in logic/time.rs). | **R10** Sporadic release and MIT enforcement (R10.1 to R10.9, Phase P1).<br>When an event arrives for a sporadic Task, the Kernel releases the Task only if no Release is waiting and at least one minimum inter-arrival time (MIT) has passed since the last one; otherwise it holds the event to the end of the MIT or drops it, records a violation, and applies the Partition's fault response once the violations pass a declared threshold. | The Kernel's intake function decides accept, defer or discard from the Task's last accepted instant and its MIT, counts the violation against the source's Partition, and masks the source for one MIT after every outcome (crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/kernel.rs, `Kernel::intake`; the timing record in logic/time.rs). | **R17** DMA isolation (R17.1 to R17.7, Phase P1).<br>A peripheral that moves data by itself (EasyDMA), bypassing memory protection, may only read and write its own Partition's ordinary memory; a request for any other buffer is refused before a byte moves, and a Partition's transfers are stopped before its memory is re-initialized. | A Partition cannot write its DMA peripheral's pointer and count registers: its view maps that peripheral read-only. About the answer only, not about the registers written.<br>`dma_request_core` (Verus, `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs:1323`): The Kernel's invariant is preserved and the Job stack does not grow. The request is accepted exactly when `dma_accepts` holds of the state it was called in. If accepted, the Kernel's state is as before and the model's list of programmed transfers has one more entry: this channel's pointer register, the buffer, this channel's count register, the length. If refused, that list is unchanged. The record of register writes made for Partitions is unchanged either way, as are the interrupt mask level, the MPU view and the global interrupt mask.<br>`dma_accepts` (Verus, `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs:1306`): A request for channel i is acceptable when the channel exists, a Job is executing, the channel's peripheral belongs to the Partition of the Job on top, that Partition exists, and the buffer is DMA-permitted memory of that Partition.<br>`dma_write_core` (Verus, `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs:1398`): The Kernel's invariant is preserved. If it is refused, the record is unchanged. Either way the record of programmed transfers is unchanged: this service never programs a transfer.<br>`dma_reg_unmediated` (Verus, `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs:1389`): A register is unmediated for channel i when, for every channel whose pointer register lies in the same 4 KiB window as channel i's, it is not that channel's pointer register, count register, or either list-mode register.<br>`bytes_are_out_of_reach_while_a_transfer_is_outstanding` (Kani, `crates/rsk/src/lib.rs:1262`): For every sequence of four operations on one buffer (read its bytes, lend it and keep or drop the transfer, take a kept transfer back, drop a kept transfer), with the peripheral's enable register and STOPPED event set to any values before each: the bytes are handed out exactly when no accepted transfer is outstanding; R17.1 and R17.2: the request function is proven to accept a request exactly when the channel belongs to the executing Job's Partition and the buffer passes the test; an accepted request programs that channel's two registers with that buffer and nothing else, a refused one programs nothing; the register write behind it is checked to write those two registers only; and every byte of a permitted buffer is proven to lie in the Partition's own RAM above its stack, given the hardware rule HW-15. | **R18** Temporal isolation and Budget enforcement (R18.1 to R18.9, Phase P1).<br>Each Job's execution time is counted against its Budget, an overrun is detected and answered as its Partition declared, and as a result a Partition that keeps to its Budgets meets the response times the Analyzer computed whatever lower-criticality Partitions do. | The Kernel charges the executing Job the processor cycles between switch points and arms a timer event for the instant its Budget would run out; the event reports the Overrun and applies the response (`Kernel::timer_event`, `budget_event`, `settle` in crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/kernel.rs; the cycle counter and the charge points in crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs). Every periodic Task due at the entry's reading has its Release served and every other is left alone. In the safe state nothing changes.<br>`budget_event` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/kernel.rs:3122`): The event charges no account. If an Overrun was already reported for this Job, the log, the accounts and the scheduler are unchanged. If the Job on top is this Task's, is unreported, and its account exceeds its Budget, then afterwards the Overrun is marked reported, or the account has been reset because the response ended the Partition.<br>`settle` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/kernel.rs:3940`): The last step of every Kernel entry changes nothing but, at most, the executing Job's Budget slot; it returns the Task the scheduling rule admits, if any; and whenever a Task is admitted, no Budget event is left armed.<br>`property18_kernel` (Lean, `proofs/aeneas/lean/Sched/KRun.lean:721`): Take the Analyzer's result as the compiled code computes it. | **R39** Static, heap-free, executor-free implementation (R39.1 to R39.4, Phase P4).<br>Message passing between Tasks uses fixed, statically allocated buffers with no heap and no async runtime, each operation has a bounded execution time, and a buffer behaves as a first-in, first-out queue of its declared capacity. | Each Endpoint channel is a ring of fixed-size slots in Kernel-owned storage; the index arithmetic is `endpoint::Fifo` (crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/endpoint.rs) and the copies in and out are word copies by the Kernel (crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs).<br>Statements in: `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/endpoint.rs`.<br>6 source files cite a criterion of R39 in the matrix (1 of the files above among them). | `push` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/endpoint.rs:60`): On a well-formed queue of the given capacity: if it returns a slot, the queue was not full, the slot is the next position after the last, and the queue's sequence is the old one with that slot appended; if it returns nothing, the queue was full and is unchanged.<br>`pop` (Verus, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/endpoint.rs:87`): If it returns a slot, the queue was not empty, the slot is the oldest, and the queue's sequence is the old one without its first element; if it returns nothing, the queue was empty and is unchanged. | **Proven:** Verus (2) of the statements in column 3.<br>**Tested (host):** `property20` (projection and buffer bound).<br>Allocation rows: P-09.<br>Evidence_Items naming a criterion of R39: none in the store. | **Weaker.** The queue of slot indices is proven to be a first-in, first-out sequence: a push appends the next slot unless the queue is full, a pop removes the oldest unless it is empty, and a refused operation changes nothing. The step from slots to message contents is the Kernel's copy, which is checked by Kani to stay in bounds and round-trip its words, and the model records only each message's first word. R39.3's execution-time bounds are measured. R39.1 (no heap, no executor) is the Link_Checker's and the lint's. |
| **R40** Ceiling integration and message-driven release (R40.1 to R40.6, Phase P4).<br>Endpoint buffers are Kernel-owned Resources under the ceiling protocol, a message can release a sporadic Task subject to its MIT, send and receive never wait, and a full buffer is an error reported to the Health_Monitor. | Send and receive are supervisor calls served at the Kernel's level, so each is one indivisible step for every Task (`endpoint_send_core`, `endpoint_recv_core` in crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs); a send to a receive role bound as a Release_Source goes through the same intake as an interrupt (see R10); the Analyzer counts each operation in the Task's execution and blocking terms.<br>Statements in: `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs`, `crates/rsk-logic/src/logic/endpoint.rs`.<br>41 source files cite a criterion of R40 in the matrix (2 of the files above among them). | `endpoint_send_core` (Verus, `crates/rsk-kernel/src/arch/cm4/entry.rs:2229`): The Kernel's and the entry code's invariants are preserved and the Job stack does not grow; the interrupt mask level, MPU view and global mask are unchanged. If the send is accepted, the message's first word is appended to the channel's label sequence. If it is not accepted, nothing is written into the Endpoint storage and every channel's queue is as it was. A receive that is not refused leaves the Kernel's state as it was and delivers the oldest label.
